description: Rules the specification itself declares non-testable. Every entry must name a FeatureId whose `Conformance` cell is NOT_COVERED, explain why no executable case can exist, cite the normative text, and state the condition under which the exemption must be re-examined. `python tools/features_coverage.py --strict` fails if an entry is malformed, unknown, stale or hides an uncited rule.

exemptions.reason: La ligne declare elle-meme « pass : aucun (oracle absent) » et sa colonne Conformance vaut NOT_COVERED. La machine abstraite du noyau pur n'a aucune forme executable : MACH-1.4 fixe son etat a NOT_IMPLEMENTED et interdit de citer un resultat machine comme preuve. Inventer un cas reviendrait a inventer un oracle, ce qui est precisement le faux PASS que T2 doit interdire.
exemptions.review_condition: Revoquer cette exemption des qu'une machine abstraite executable existe (MACH-1.4 quitte NOT_IMPLEMENTED) ou si la ligne F-META-006 obtient une forme executable ; la couverture stricte doit alors repasser a 188/188 sans exemption. Reexamen obligatoire au plus tard le 2027-02-12 (90 jours apres l'approbation humaine du 2026-11-12).
exemptions.approved_by: Rwanbt (responsable du projet) — approbation explicite en session le 2026-11-12, reponse « 1 - ok » a la demande d'approbation de l'exemption F-META-006.

line_coverage_exemptions.owner_decision: S5, APPROUVÉ par le responsable, 2026-11-14 : « Objectif de couverture : 100 % lignes et régions du CODE PRODUIT, hors modules #[cfg(test)] et hors chemins inatteignables documentés un par un. » Ce bloc est la liste « un par un ».
line_coverage_exemptions.policy: Une entrée n'est admise que si AUCUNE entrée de programme acceptée n'emprunte la ligne, et chaque entrée porte la preuve (test qui exécute le refus, mesure, ou argument statique sur le parseur/checker). Une entrée n'est PAS une auto-approbation : elle reste `PENDING_HUMAN_APPROVAL`, n'est jamais défalquée du chiffre brut, et le chiffre « objectif S5 » est publié séparément. Une entrée sans preuve est interdite ; une ligne inatteignable non listée reste une dette de couverture comptée. Ce fichier ne modifie aucun seuil (`tools/coverage_thresholds.json`).
line_coverage_exemptions.measured_on: 2026-11-14 (vague 3, agent F), branche goal/wave-3 + branche wave3/f-coverage-mutation
line_coverage_exemptions.command: cargo llvm-cov -p ravum-lang-sema -p ravum-lang-codegen --json --output-path target/cov-all.json ; python tools/coverage_product_split.py --input target/cov-all.json ; python tools/coverage_report.py --input target/cov-all.json --gap

Coverage is measured on a debug build (`cargo llvm-cov` without `--release`), so the line cannot be covered by any test in the measured profile.

entries.summary: Ownership walk of a range without a start or an end.
entries.why_unreachable: After a parse without error the only range in a program is the outermost expression of a `for` iterator: `parse_range` consumes `in_for_iter`, so every other range (nested in the iterator, an operand, anywhere else) is E-UNSUPPORTED-RANGE (parser/exprs.rs, parser/primary.rs). `check_for_range` then refuses a range without both bounds (E-TYP-RANGE, typeck/control.rs), and ownership, effects, traps and the back end only run on a program that checked. The implicit `None` side of `if let Some(start|end)` is therefore never taken past typeck.
entries.review_condition: Des plages ouvertes (`a..`, `..b`) acceptées par Core.

entries.summary: `pop_scope` or `declare_slot` with no open scope.
entries.why_unreachable: `check_fn` pushes the function scope before declaring its parameters and pops it last; every other `push_scope` (block, branch, arm, loop) is paired with a `pop_scope` in the same function, so the scope stack is never empty while a slot is declared or a scope is closed.
entries.review_condition: Un `pop_scope` hors d'une paire.

entries.summary: `&&`/`||` whose left operand diverged and whose right operand did not.
entries.why_unreachable: Typeck requires both operands of `&&` and `||` to be `bool` and refuses a `!` operand (E-TYP-MISMATCH "`&&` requires `bool` operands, found `!` and `bool`"); ownership only runs on a program that checked.
entries.proof: crates/ravum-lang-sema/src/typeck (binary operators); check.rs runs ownership only without errors.
evidence: ravum-lang build of `(return true) && c`: E-TYP-MISMATCH
entries.review_condition: Des opérandes `!` acceptés par `&&`/`||`.

entries.summary: An assignment whose target is not a place.
entries.why_unreachable: The parser refuses an assignment whose left side is not a name, a field, an index or a dereference (E-PARSE-EXPECTED "left side of an assignment must be a place"), and `eval_place_expr` returns a place for each of those forms.
entries.review_condition: Des cibles d'affectation qui ne sont pas des places.

entries.summary: A `break` joined into the exit of a `while` whose condition diverged.
entries.why_unreachable: When the condition diverges the body is analysed through `analyze_dead`, which restores `loop_stack`: its `break`s are discarded, so `ctx.breaks` is empty whenever the exit starts as `None` (same mechanism as E-LINE-OWN-LOOP-EXIT-BREAK-AFTER-DIVERGING-HEADER).
entries.review_condition: Une analyse du corps mort qui conserve ses `break`.

entries.summary: A non-function member of an `impl` when collecting the functions to analyse.
entries.why_unreachable: `resolve_impl` reports E-RES-IMPL-UNKNOWN for every non-`fn` member of an `impl`, and ownership does not run after a resolution error (same proof as E-LINE-TYP-IMPL-NON-FN-MEMBER).
entries.review_condition: Des `const` ou modules associés.

entries.summary: Two paths of the same slot whose first incompatible steps are of different kinds.
entries.why_unreachable: Both paths start at the same slot and agree up to that position, so the step applies to the same type: a struct takes a field step, a tuple a tuple step, an array, `Vec` or slice an index step, a reference a deref step (handled above). Two literal or opaque indexes are compatible, so the only incompatible pairs left are the ones matched above.
entries.proof: crates/ravum-lang-sema/src/own/state.rs `step_compatible`, `diverges_disjoint`; place steps are built from typed projections in own/checker_a.rs `eval_place_expr`.
entries.review_condition: Des projections de genres différents sur un même type.

entries.summary: A place whose slot has no state or no declaration info.
entries.why_unreachable: Every `Place` the checker builds starts from `lookup`, which only returns a slot of a binding in scope. Each `declare_slot` (function parameters, `let`, match-arm bindings, `for` bindings) is immediately followed by an insertion into `state.slots`, and `pop_scope` removes a slot from `slots` and `state.slots` together. `join` keeps the union of both states, and every state snapshot that is put back (`analyze_dead`, loop entry, branches) was taken while the scope of the slot it lacks was closed or is re-filled (`for` bindings). A slot in scope therefore always has a state and an info.
evidence: crates/ravum-lang-sema/tests/own_partial_facts.rs (the phase never panics on incomplete facts)
entries.review_condition: Une liaison créée sans état (motifs à plusieurs liaisons, fermetures).

entries.summary: A `break` joined into the exit of a `for` whose iterator diverged.
entries.why_unreachable: When the iterator diverges the body is analysed through `analyze_dead`, which saves and restores `loop_stack`: the `break`s it records are discarded, so `ctx.breaks` is empty whenever the exit starts as `None`.
entries.review_condition: Une analyse du corps mort qui conserve ses `break`.

entries.summary: `element_write` meeting a moved path that the written place extends.
entries.why_unreachable: `write_place` calls `check_availability(Access::Write)` first and returns when it fails; a write to a place extending a moved path is refused there (E-OWN-USE-AFTER-MOVE), so `element_write` never sees that relation.
entries.review_condition: Un `element_write` appelé hors de `write_place`.

entries.summary: Moving out through an index of a slice value.
entries.why_unreachable: A slice exists only behind a reference, and `auto_deref` puts a `Deref` step before its index; `perform_move` refuses any move whose path has a `Deref` before the last step (E-OWN-MOVE-OUT-OF-BORROW) before it looks at the indexed type.
entries.review_condition: Des tranches par valeur.

entries.summary: Skipping the debug-only cross-check of element paths (`if cfg!(debug_assertions)`).
entries.why_unreachable: The branch that skips `cross_check` is taken only in a release build; coverage is measured on the default debug profile, where `cfg!(debug_assertions)` is always true.
entries.proof: `if cfg!(debug_assertions) { self.cross_check(expr, root); }` in `walk_path`; same reasoning as E-LINE-EMIT-RELEASE-ONLY-OWNERSHIP-GUARD.
entries.review_condition: Une mesure de couverture en profil release.

entries.summary: `slot_of` on a tuple or field step whose base is not a tuple or a struct.
entries.why_unreachable: `slot_of` is only asked about the steps after the first fixed-size array index, while each previous step still had a slot. The base of such a step is then an array element, a tuple item or a struct field, and typeck types `x.0` / `x.f` only on a tuple / struct or a reference to one. A reference cannot be stored in an array, tuple or struct in Core (E-OWN-REF-ESCAPE), so the base is the tuple or struct itself.
entries.review_condition: Des références stockables dans un agrégat.

entries.summary: `planned_path` on a node that is not an element path.
entries.why_unreachable: A node gets a `PathMode` only from `plan`: a move or borrow access is recorded by `walk_path` after `element_path(expr)` returned `Some`, and `planned_path` calls the same pure function on the same expression and facts. A re-initialisation target is recorded only when `OwnFacts::element_reinit` holds it, which `element_write` sets only for a place with an array index, and that index is on a fixed-size array (a `Vec` element cannot be moved out, E-OWN-PARTIAL-MOVE).
entries.review_condition: Un mode de chemin attribué hors de `walk_path`.

entries.summary: Moving out through an index of something that is not a fixed-size array.
entries.why_unreachable: Past the first fixed-size array index the moved value is consumed step by step; an index of a `Vec` or a slice there would move a `Vec` element out, which the ownership checker refuses (E-OWN-PARTIAL-MOVE "déplacement d'un élément de `Vec` par indexation interdit").
evidence: ravum-lang build of `let x = a[0].v[0];` with `v: Vec<String>`: E-OWN-PARTIAL-MOVE
entries.review_condition: Le déplacement hors d'un `Vec` par indexation.

entries.summary: A re-initialised element whose path goes past the constant run.
entries.why_unreachable: `element_write` records a re-initialisation only when no opaque index follows the first array index, and a `Vec` element is never moved out (E-OWN-PARTIAL-MOVE). Field and tuple steps always have a slot (E-LINE-EMIT-PATHS-SLOT-NON-AGGREGATE), so the constant run stops only at a literal index past the end of a fixed-size array, which the branch just above lowers to a run-time panic.
entries.review_condition: Une réinitialisation à travers un index non constant.

entries.summary: The coverage check giving up past `MAX_COVERAGE_DEPTH` (1024) levels.
entries.why_unreachable: Each recursion of the coverage check descends one level of the scrutinee type, and typeck resolves no type nested deeper than `MAX_RESOLVE_DEPTH` (1024, typeck/helpers.rs), which equals the guard.
entries.review_condition: Une borne de résolution des types supérieure à celle de la couverture.

entries.summary: An `Option`, `Result` or tuple scrutinee matched by a pattern that is neither a constructor nor irrefutable.
entries.why_unreachable: A constant cannot hold an `Option`, a `Result` or a tuple (`const A: Option<i32> = Some(1);`, `Ok(1)` and `(1, 2)` are E-TYP-CONST), so the only patterns that type-check against such a scrutinee are its constructors (`Some`/`None`, `Ok`/`Err`, a tuple pattern) and the irrefutable ones, which `patterns_exhaustive` has already accepted before this match.
evidence: ravum-lang build of `const A: Option<i32> = Some(1);`, `const P: (i32, i32) = (1, 2);`: E-TYP-CONST
entries.review_condition: Des constantes d'`Option`, de `Result` ou de tuple.

entries.summary: A pattern recorded in `variant_pats` that is neither a path nor a variant pattern.
entries.why_unreachable: `variant_pats` is filled only by `check_path_pattern` and `check_variant_pattern` (typeck/aggregates.rs), for `PatKind::Path` and `PatKind::Variant`; both functions are reached only for a pattern found in it.
entries.review_condition: Un autre genre de motif enregistré comme variante.

entries.summary: A binding identity recorded for an expression whose resolution is not a local (debug cross-check).
entries.why_unreachable: The ownership checker publishes a binding identity only in `eval_place_expr`, for a slot found by `path_local_slot` or `lookup("self")`. With the facts of a checked program every path has a resolution, and `path_local_slot` returns a slot only for `Resolution::Local`; `self` is always resolved to a local by typeck (`check_self_value`).
entries.review_condition: Une identité de liaison publiée hors de `eval_place_expr`.

entries.summary: `syntactic_place` on `self` or a single-segment path that does not resolve to a local (debug cross-check).
entries.why_unreachable: `syntactic_place` is called on the expressions of `OwnFacts::place` and on the bases of their projections, and by the element-path cross-check on roots of projections. Every recorded place starts at a local slot, `self` always resolves to a local, and a projection rooted at a constant or function does not type-check (constants are scalars or `&str`: E-TYP-CONST for aggregates; fields and indexes of those are E-TYP-* errors).
entries.review_condition: Des constantes agrégées.

entries.summary: The user `main` or a test function without an entry in `index.fns`.
entries.why_unreachable: `Index::build` records an `FnEntry` for every function item it walks; `user_main` is filtered to raw items of kind `Fn` and the tests are collected from function items during the same walk.
entries.review_condition: Un `main` ou un test hors de l'index.

entries.summary: A module node missing from the index.
entries.why_unreachable: `emit_module` walks the same module tree as `Index::walk_module`, which registers every module it enters (the root and each `ItemKind::Mod`) before walking its items.
entries.review_condition: Des modules émis hors de l'arbre indexé.

entries.summary: `register_source` refusing the manifest of a dependency.
entries.why_unreachable: A dependency manifest is registered under `<key>/ravum.toml`, and the key must equal the target's `package.name` (E-MOD-DEPENDENCY otherwise), so one canonical manifest always comes with the same display name and an existing id is reused; a new id comes from a counter that only grows, so `add_at` never meets a taken id.
evidence: ravum-lang check of `other = { path = "../util" }`: E-MOD-DEPENDENCY "dependency key `other` does not match the target `package.name`"
entries.review_condition: Des clés de dépendance différentes du nom du paquet.

entries.summary: `fs::canonicalize` failing on a dependency directory whose components were just checked.
entries.why_unreachable: Every component of the dependency path was checked with `symlink_metadata` just above: it exists and is not a symbolic link. `canonicalize` can then fail only if the tree changes between the two system calls (a concurrent removal), which no test can schedule deterministically.
entries.review_condition: Une résolution qui ne vérifie plus chaque composant.

entries.summary: A canonical dependency directory outside the package parent.
entries.why_unreachable: The lexical pass refuses any `..` that climbs above the package parent (E-MOD-PATH-ESCAPE), every component is then checked not to be a symbolic link, and `pkg_dir` is itself canonical (the root is canonicalized in loader/files.rs, a dependency directory is the canonical path returned here). The canonical path is therefore the lexical one, which stays inside the parent.
evidence: ravum-lang check of a package reached through a symlinked directory with a `../util` dependency: accepted
entries.review_condition: Un répertoire de paquet non canonique.

entries.summary: An inline module without a name.
entries.why_unreachable: Only the root module of a file has `name: None`; the parser builds every `mod name { ... }` with `Some(name)` (an unnamed `mod { }` is E-PARSE-EXPECTED), and `expand_module` only reaches inline modules through `ItemKind::Mod` items.
entries.review_condition: Des modules anonymes.

entries.summary: `fs::canonicalize` failing on a module file that was just found.
entries.why_unreachable: The candidate was just found to exist (`is_file`/`is_dir`) and checked by `check_lexical_no_symlinks`; `canonicalize` can then fail only if the tree changes between the system calls, which no test can schedule deterministically.
entries.review_condition: Une recherche de module qui ne vérifie plus l'existence.

entries.summary: A dependency whose crate root fails to load after the graph accepted it.
entries.why_unreachable: Before `load_crates` merges a dependency, `collect_dependencies` refused a missing or symlinked `src/lib.rv`, and the package digest read every file of the dependency under the same size and encoding limits (E-LIMIT-FILE-SIZE, E-UNSUPPORTED-TOKEN). `load_crate_root` can then fail only if the tree changes in between.
entries.review_condition: Un chargement des dépendances sans graphe ni empreinte préalables.

entries.summary: Fallback arms after a namespace lookup in the value-path resolver (`is a struct, not a value`, `unknown` for a non-module in `Ns::Module`).
entries.why_unreachable: `World::register` and `insert_import` assert (debug) that a symbol is stored in its own namespace (`sym.ns() == ns`); the whole sema test suite and the conformance corpus run with that assertion. A lookup in `Ns::Module` therefore returns only `Sym::Module` / `Sym::BuiltinModule`, in `Ns::Value` only `Sym::Fn` / `Sym::Const` / `Sym::BuiltinFn`, in `Ns::Type` only `Sym::Struct` / `Sym::Enum`.
entries.proof: `World::register` and `insert_import` assert (debug) that a symbol is stored in its own namespace (`sym.ns() == ns`); the whole sema test suite and the conformance corpus run with that assertion. A lookup in `Ns::Module` therefore returns only `Sym::Module` / `Sym::BuiltinModule`, in `Ns::Value` only `Sym::Fn` / `Sym::Const` / `Sym::BuiltinFn`, in `Ns::Type` only `Sym::Struct` / `Sym::Enum`.
evidence: cargo test -p ravum-lang-sema (995 passed, 0 failed with the assertions)
entries.review_condition: Un symbole stocké dans un autre espace de noms que le sien (par exemple un alias de type dans les valeurs).

entries.why_unreachable: `World::register` and `insert_import` assert (debug) that a symbol is stored in its own namespace (`sym.ns() == ns`); the whole sema test suite and the conformance corpus run with that assertion. A lookup in `Ns::Module` therefore returns only `Sym::Module` / `Sym::BuiltinModule`, in `Ns::Value` only `Sym::Fn` / `Sym::Const` / `Sym::BuiltinFn`, in `Ns::Type` only `Sym::Struct` / `Sym::Enum`.
entries.proof: `World::register` and `insert_import` assert (debug) that a symbol is stored in its own namespace (`sym.ns() == ns`); the whole sema test suite and the conformance corpus run with that assertion. A lookup in `Ns::Module` therefore returns only `Sym::Module` / `Sym::BuiltinModule`, in `Ns::Value` only `Sym::Fn` / `Sym::Const` / `Sym::BuiltinFn`, in `Ns::Type` only `Sym::Struct` / `Sym::Enum`. `nominal_type` is called only with a symbol found in `Ns::Type`.

entries.summary: Same namespace invariant in the `use` resolver (anchors and tail).
entries.why_unreachable: `World::register` and `insert_import` assert (debug) that a symbol is stored in its own namespace (`sym.ns() == ns`); the whole sema test suite and the conformance corpus run with that assertion. A lookup in `Ns::Module` therefore returns only `Sym::Module` / `Sym::BuiltinModule`, in `Ns::Value` only `Sym::Fn` / `Sym::Const` / `Sym::BuiltinFn`, in `Ns::Type` only `Sym::Struct` / `Sym::Enum`.
entries.proof: `World::register` and `insert_import` assert (debug) that a symbol is stored in its own namespace (`sym.ns() == ns`); the whole sema test suite and the conformance corpus run with that assertion. A lookup in `Ns::Module` therefore returns only `Sym::Module` / `Sym::BuiltinModule`, in `Ns::Value` only `Sym::Fn` / `Sym::Const` / `Sym::BuiltinFn`, in `Ns::Type` only `Sym::Struct` / `Sym::Enum`. `UseTarget::Symbol` is built only for items of `Ns::Value`/`Ns::Type`; modules go through `UseTarget::Module`.
entries.review_condition: Idem.

entries.summary: A value path with no segment, and a path that ends while the cursor is still on a module or a type.
entries.why_unreachable: `Parser::parse_path` pushes a segment before it can stop, except on its error branch, which reports `E-PARSE-EXPECTED` ("expected path segment"); a program with a parse error never reaches the checker (the loader fails, `ravum-lang check` exits). Every loop turn on the last segment returns, so the `index >= len` check at the top of the loop is reached only by an empty tail.
entries.proof: `rv check` on `fn f(x: crate) { }` and `let x = crate;` reports `E-PARSE-EXPECTED: expected path segment` and stops before resolution.
entries.review_condition: Un chemin vide accepté par le parseur, ou une boucle de résolution qui continuerait après le dernier segment.

entries.summary: Same two shapes in the type-path resolver.
entries.why_unreachable: `Parser::parse_path` pushes a segment before it can stop, except on its error branch, which reports `E-PARSE-EXPECTED` ("expected path segment"); a program with a parse error never reaches the checker (the loader fails, `ravum-lang check` exits).
entries.review_condition: Idem.

entries.summary: Privacy refusal of the first segment of a value path, looked up in the current module.
entries.why_unreachable: An item reached by a single name is looked up in the current module: its own items are visible there whatever their `pub`, and a `use` binding is `Vis::Private` with `def_module` = the importing module (MOD-4.1/4.3, fix 989a96b), hence visible too.
entries.proof: An item reached by a single name is looked up in the current module: its own items are visible there whatever their `pub`, and a `use` binding is `Vis::Private` with `def_module` = the importing module (MOD-4.1/4.3, fix 989a96b), hence visible too. Cross-module privacy is checked on the later segments (tests `a_private_module_cannot_be_crossed`, `mutation_gaps`).
entries.review_condition: `pub use`, ou une recherche du premier segment hors du module courant.

entries.summary: Same refusal for a single-name type.
entries.why_unreachable: An item reached by a single name is looked up in the current module: its own items are visible there whatever their `pub`, and a `use` binding is `Vis::Private` with `def_module` = the importing module (MOD-4.1/4.3, fix 989a96b), hence visible too.

entries.summary: `find_unqualified_variant` answering `Option`/`Result` for `Some`/`None`/`Ok`/`Err`.
entries.why_unreachable: `resolve_value_path` returns for these four names (`BuiltinCtor`/`BuiltinConst`) before it calls `find_unqualified_variant`, and the other caller resolves a user enum's variants.
entries.proof: crates/ravum-lang-sema/src/resolve/paths.rs single-segment branch: `"Some" | "None" | "Ok" | "Err"` arms precede the variant lookup.
entries.review_condition: Un nouvel appelant de `find_unqualified_variant` qui ne filtre pas les constructeurs du prélude.

entries.summary: `fill_item_paths` skipping a non-item symbol of a module table, and an enum known to `nominal_kind` but missing from `world.enums`.
entries.why_unreachable: `World::build` registers only user items in the module tables (`Sym::Fn/Struct/Enum/Const/Module`, world.rs `register` calls); builtin symbols enter a module only as imports, which `fill_item_paths` does not walk. `nominal_kind` is computed from the same `world.enums`/`world.structs` maps.
entries.proof: crates/ravum-lang-sema/src/resolve/world.rs `World::build`: every `register` passes a user item symbol.
entries.review_condition: Un symbole builtin enregistré dans une table de module.

entries.summary: End of a `use` path reached while the cursor is still on a module.
entries.why_unreachable: A one-segment `use` goes through `resolve_use_single_name` (uses.rs:40) and never reaches `resolve_use_tail`; every other call starts the tail before the last segment, and the last segment always returns. `Parser::parse_path` pushes a segment before it can stop, except on its error branch, which reports `E-PARSE-EXPECTED` ("expected path segment"); a program with a parse error never reaches the checker (the loader fails, `ravum-lang check` exits).
entries.review_condition: `use m;` résolu par la queue, ou un chemin `use` vide.

entries.summary: Two distinct anchors of a bare `use` resolving to the same builtin module or function.
entries.why_unreachable: A builtin is reachable through a user module only via a `use` of that module, visible in its subtree only (MOD-4.3). The local anchor is a child of the importing module and the root anchor a child of the crate root, so the importing module is in neither subtree; a builtin root anchor is the same on both sides and returns early (`local == root`).
entries.review_condition: `pub use`, ou une ancre `use` qui ne serait pas un module enfant.

entries.summary: Copy analysis of a nominal id that is neither in `facts.structs` nor in `facts.enums`.
entries.why_unreachable: The copy analysis starts from the ids of `facts.structs`/`facts.enums` and recurses on field types resolved from the same tables; a `Type::Nominal` with any other id is the prelude `Error`, handled before.
entries.review_condition: Un type nominal sans entrée dans les tables de faits.

entries.summary: `type_generics` of an id that is neither a struct nor an enum.
entries.why_unreachable: Called with the `def` of a `Type::Nominal` resolved from `Ns::Type`, i.e. a struct or an enum of the world.
entries.review_condition: Idem.

entries.summary: A called function or enum variant without its signature or enum entry.
entries.why_unreachable: `resolve` fills `facts.fn_sigs`, `facts.structs` and `facts.enums` for every function, struct and enum item of the world (`resolve/header.rs`), and `check` runs typeck only when resolution reported no error (check.rs: `if !resolved || diags.has_errors()` returns). Every id typeck looks up comes from a resolution of the same world, so the lookup cannot miss.

entries.summary: `bind_impl_generics` on an impl whose target is not nominal, or whose argument is not a parameter.
entries.why_unreachable: `resolve_impl` returns (E-RES-IMPL-SELF-TYPE) unless the target is a nominal type of the package, and refuses (E-RES-IMPL-TARGET) unless its arguments are exactly the impl parameters in order; a method entry is only recorded after both checks.

entries.summary: `?` and `return` outside a function or inside a constant.
entries.why_unreachable: `check_const_expr` types a constant initialiser itself and refuses every form that is not a constant expression (`_` arm: E-TYP-CONST, blocks: E-TYP-CONST) without handing it to `check_expr`; `return` and `?` therefore never reach `check_return`/`check_try` with `in_const` set, and every function body sets `current_fn`.
